newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says inflation key to rates decision.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says inflation key to rates decision.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that inflation was the key determinant to a decision on monetary policy.
Costello had been asked by reporters whether the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision later on Wednesday on U.S. interest rates would have any influence on domestic monetary policy.
"Monetary policy is set with regard to a host of factors and of course we take into account in Australia international developments," said Costello.

"But...we are setting monetary policy in this country with regard to domestic factors and principally our inflation target. So it's the inflation target, which has been spelled out in the agreement between the governor (of the Reserve Bank) and me, that counts," Costello told reporters.
The RBA, which held its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, aims to keep underlying inflation averaging 2-3 percent over the course of an economic cycle.
"We always have regard to international factors, but that (inflation) is the key determinant to monetary policy in this country," Costello said.
Annual underlying inflation growth stood at 2.1 percent in the March quarter, unchanged from the previous quarter.

The Federal Reserve Open Market Committee finishes a two-day meeting on Wednesday and there has been speculation it could sanction a U.S. rate hike. Such an increase would take official U.S. rates above those in Australia, which some analysts felt could limit the RBA's room to ease policy here.
